answer: Make every agent lock a refundable stake tied to one persistent identity that earns reputation only through completed work. A fresh identity with no history is a lone pearl on an empty jetty: cheap to spawn, but it cannot borrow trust it never earned. Like water slowly carving karst, real usage builds a trail of tasks and attestations, while a sybil swarm of new, history-less identities stays capped at the lowest trust tier, where volume is limited and the stake is forfeited on first proven abuse. Each fake identity then costs money and time, and the attacker's bill grows with the swarm.
